kind.d: Scaled-down skateboard ridden with the fingers, about 96 mm long, with a plywood deck, metal trucks and urethane wheels.

x.d: First mass-produced fingerboard not meant for figurines or accessories.
Best-known toy fingerboard brand, with licensed skate-brand graphics; video games followed in 2000 and 2001.
German professional-grade fingerboards, trucks and ramps by Blackriver Ramps, founded 1999.
American fingerboard brand founded by Mike Schneider in 2003; also a US distributor of Blackriver.
